verdict.summary: Snowflake is accelerating where it matters, but the equity discounts years of successful consumption growth. Q1 FY27 product revenue rose 34% to $1.334B, RPO advanced 38% to $9.21B and net revenue retention held at 126%. Cortex and Snowpark raise paid compute only when governed workloads reach production. GAAP operating margin was negative 23.4% versus positive 11.9% non-GAAP, while convertible instruments add roughly 15M shares to guidance. The dated valuation is 19.7x FY27 product revenue with a 0.9% annualized adjusted-FCF yield. September 2 earnings veto execution. After review, Snowflake must clear $334.60; the $330.7999 Aug. 13 low defines risk, with $340.50 and $341.95 as observed August highs. A product beat without stable NRR, margin and diluted-share discipline does not justify entry.

business.overview:
Snowflake charges primarily for product consumption across data warehousing, engineering, sharing, applications and governance. Product revenue moves with compute and storage usage rather than contracted seats. RPO supplies visibility, while net revenue retention shows whether existing customers expand workloads after optimization.

Cortex AI, Snowpark and native applications connect AI demand to Snowflake credits. The financial transmission occurs when governed enterprise data stays inside Snowflake and production agents repeatedly invoke models, queries and pipelines. A proof of concept can raise activity without producing sustained consumption or protecting product gross margin.

The failure path is renewed optimization, migration toward hyperscaler-native services, or slow RPO conversion. Cloud expense, stock compensation and convertible dilution can keep per-share economics behind product growth. September 2 results must refresh product guidance, NRR and cash-margin assumptions before the displayed setup can be used.

The decisive quarterly bridge runs from signed commitments to consumed credits. If RPO expands while product growth or NRR fades, the backlog is lengthening rather than strengthening, and the current premium has no operating support.
business.moat: Snowflake's moat is its governed cross-cloud data layer, separation of storage and compute, and network effects from secure data sharing and native applications. Moving production pipelines, policies and shared datasets is disruptive. Hyperscalers still control infrastructure and can bundle competing warehouses, databases and AI services.

earnings.beatNote: Q1 FY27 revenue was $1.39B, up 33%, and product revenue was $1.334B, up 34%. RPO increased 38% to $9.21B, NRR was 126%, and customers generating more than $1M of trailing product revenue rose 29% to 779. GAAP operating loss was $326.2M, or 23.4% of revenue; non-GAAP operating income was $165.8M, or 11.9%. Adjusted free cash flow was $265.5M. Management guided Q2 product revenue to $1.415B-$1.420B and FY27 product revenue to $5.84B. The non-GAAP outlook includes about 15M convertible-related shares.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: Snowflake reported approximately 346.6M shares outstanding and a Q1 diluted weighted-average count of 345.391M. Management's fiscal outlook includes roughly 15M convertible-related shares; assuming those are incremental to the current basic count produces a minimum potential 361.6M denominator. Because the filing does not reconcile overlap with treasury-method awards, the exact theoretical fully diluted count remains unavailable. Cash of $2.95B is close to $2.77B of reported debt, so liquidity does not erase dilution. Product revenue and adjusted free cash flow must compound after employee compensation and conversion effects.

filings.finding: The Q1 FY27 10-Q supports $1.39B revenue, the $326.2M GAAP operating loss, liquidity and convertible-share accounting; no ATM, primary common sale, secondary offering or new debt financing is identified.
The FY2026 10-K establishes the consumption model, stock-compensation burden, convertible obligations and annual risk factors; it is a periodic report, not evidence of fresh equity or debt issuance.

The July 16 Form 8-K grants CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy 1,000,000 performance stock units across five tranches with $324-$531 stock-price hurdles and two-to-seven-year performance periods. It is contingent compensation and potential employee dilution, not an ATM, primary cash raise, secondary sale or debt financing.
